//dockerfilePath: Relative to the REPOSITORY ROOT, which is also the build context.
The Dockerfile copies Assets/Scripts/Rules and Assets/StreamingAssets, both of
which live outside server/. So the context has to be the root, and this file
sits at the root so Railway uses the root. Moving either one breaks the build
with a COPY error naming a path that plainly exists.
The previous host's config got this wrong in exactly that way.

//numReplicas: A single small machine serves three hundred players of an idle game
comfortably -- measured, 763 requests a second with a settle p99 of 61ms. More
replicas would also multiply the bill, which is the thing this whole host
//healthcheckPath: /readyz touches the database, so it answers the question the platform is
actually asking: should traffic be routed here. /healthz is liveness only and
is what the container's own HEALTHCHECK uses -- a server that cannot reach
Postgres is still alive, and restarting it would turn a database blip into a
//restartPolicyType: Restart on failure, but bounded. An unbounded retry against a misconfiguration
-- a bad connection string, a missing JWT secret -- is a container that burns
compute forever while never becoming healthy, and compute is billed.
